questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I : The class name Reptilia refers to creeping or crawling mode of locomotion.
Statement II : All organisms belonging to Reptilia have three chambered heart.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.solution:
Statement I is correct because the class name Reptilia is derived from the Latin word 'repere' or 'reptum', which means to creep or crawl, referring to their mode of locomotion.

Statement II is incorrect because while most reptiles have a three-chambered heart (two atria and one partially divided ventricle), crocodiles are an exception and possess a four-chambered heart.

Therefore, Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.

Answer: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.q:
Select the incorrect statements from the following :
A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete.
B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms.
C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes.
D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes.
E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.
Choose the answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Statement A is correct. Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system with a single opening that serves as both mouth and anus.

Statement B is incorrect. Adult echinoderms exhibit radial symmetry, whereas their larvae exhibit bilateral symmetry.

Statement C is correct. Aschelminthes possess a pseudocoelom, where the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm but is present as scattered pouches.

Statement D is correct. In members of the class Chondrichthyes, the notochord is persistent throughout life.

Statement E is incorrect. Members of the class Reptilia are poikilotherms (cold-blooded) and cannot maintain a constant body temperature.

Therefore, the incorrect statements are B and E.

Answer: B and E only

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a characteristic of chordates ?
questions.solution:
The fundamental characteristics of chordates include the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord, paired pharyngeal gill slits, and a post-anal tail.

The presence of pharyngeal gill slits is a defining feature of chordates at some stage of their life cycle. Therefore, the absence of gills is not a characteristic of chordates.

Answer: Absence of gills

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match List I with List II :
List IList II
A. MolluscsI. Pulmonary respiration only
B. ReptilesII. Branchial respiration
C. Adult amphibiansIII. Cellular respiration
D. AmoebaIV. Pulmonary and Cutaneous respiration

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Molluscs primarily use gills for respiration, which is known as branchial respiration. Thus, A matches II.

Reptiles rely exclusively on lungs for gas exchange, which is termed pulmonary respiration. Thus, B matches I.

Adult amphibians, such as frogs, can respire through both their lungs and their moist skin, utilizing pulmonary and cutaneous respiration. Thus, C matches IV.

Amoeba is a unicellular organism that exchanges gases directly across its cell membrane via simple diffusion, which corresponds to cellular respiration. Thus, D matches III.

The correct matching is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

Answer: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed :
A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage.
B. Ectoparasitic, as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth.
C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but $7$ pairs of gill slits were present.
Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters ?
questions.solution:
The given characteristics belong to the class Cyclostomata.

Members of this class are ectoparasites on some fishes. They have an elongated body bearing $6-15$ pairs of gill slits for respiration.

Cyclostomes have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws.

Their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

Cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous.

Petromyzon (Lamprey) and Myxine (Hagfish) are examples of class Cyclostomata.

Scoliodon belongs to class Chondrichthyes.

Exocoetus belongs to class Osteichthyes.

Branchiostoma belongs to subphylum Cephalochordata.

Thus, Petromyzon sp. fits best with the given characters.

Answer: Petromyzon sp.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal?
questions.solution:
In pseudocoelomates, the body cavity is not entirely lined with mesoderm, instead, mesodermal tissue is present along the body wall but not towards the gut.
- Schizocoelomates are animals whose coelom or body cavity develops middle from a split in the mesoderm, the middle germ layer of the embryo.
- In acoelomates, coelom is absent.

Spongocoel is a central cavity found in Sponges.

Thus, all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.

questions.q: Select the set of fishes which belong to the class Osteichthyes :
options: Saw fish, Fighting fish and Dog fish
Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
questions.solution:
Flying fish (Exocoetus), Angel fish (Pterophyllum), and Fighting fish (Betta) are all bony fishes belonging to the class Osteichthyes.

Devil fish (Octopus) and Cuttlefish (Sepia) belong to the phylum Mollusca.

Hagfish (Myxine) belongs to the class Cyclostomata.

Saw fish (Pristis) and Dog fish (Scoliodon) belong to the class Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes).

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion and the other is labelled as Reason.

Assertion: All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates.

Reason: Notochord is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult vertebrates.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is not correct
Assertion is not correct but Reason is correct
Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
questions.solution:
The phylum Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla i.e., Urochordata or Tunicata, Cephalochordata, and Vertebrata. So, we can clearly say that all vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates.

Thus, the Assertion is correct.

It is true that in adult vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column. This statement is telling us why all chordates are not vertebrates, but it is not telling us why other chordates are considered as chordates only but not as vertebrates.

Thus, the Reason is correct, but it is not an exact or complete explanation for the Assertion.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates, why?
options: Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in adult of some chordates.
Ventral hollow nerve cord remains throughout life in some chordates.
All chordates possess notochord throughout their life.
questions.solution:
Chordates are characterized by the presence of rod-like supporting notochord extending throughout the length of the body. Chordates are divided into three sub-phylum, i.e. Urochordates, Cephalocordates and Vertebrates.

In the vertebrates, the notochord in adults is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column. However, in Urochordates, the notochord is found only in the tail region, while in cephalochordates the notochord extends above the head in adults.

Thus, all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by
questions.solution:
Coelom: The body cavity; which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom.

Coelomates: If coelom is present, the animal is called coelomate, e.g. Annelids, Molluscs, Arthropods, Echinoderms, Hemichordates and Chordates.

Pseudoceolomates: If the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, but the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm, the animal is called pseudocoelomate, e.g. Aschelminthes.
Acoelomates: When the body cavity is absent, the animal is called acoelomate, e.g. Platyhelminthes.

SYMMETRY:

Some animals are almost asymmetrical. Their body cannot be divided into two equal halves from any plane, e.g. sponges.

Radial Symmetry: In the case of radial symmetry, any plane passing through the central axis divides the body into two identical halves, e.g. Coelenterates, Ctenophores, Echinoderms, etc.

Bilateral Symmetry: In the case of bilateral symmetry, the body can be divided into two identical halves only through a single plane, e.g. Platyhelminthes, Annelida, Arthropoda, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In the case of Poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called
questions.solution: Choanocytes (collar cells) form the lining of spongocoel in poriferans (sponges). Flagella in collar cells provide circulation to water in the water canal system. These distinctive cells line the interior body walls of sponges. These cells have a central flagellum that is surrounded by a collar of microvilli. Choanocytes are versatile cells. Their flagella beat to create the active pumping of water through the sponge, while the collars of the choanocytes are the primary areas where nutrients are absorbed into the sponge. Furthermore, in some sponges, the choanocytes develop into gametes.

questions.q: Metagenesis refers to:
options: Alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism
Occurrence a drastic change in form during post-embryonic development
Presence of a segmented body and parthenogenetic mode of reproduction
questions.solution: Body forms: Two basic body forms are found in cnidarians which differ in structure and function from one another. These are called polyp and medusa. A polyp is a cylindrical form that remains attached to the substratum (hence sessile) whereas a medusa is an umbrella-shaped and free-swimming form. Some cnidarians exist only in polyp form, e.g., Hydra, Adamsia, while some have medusa as the dominant form in their life cycle (polyp may be reduced or absent), e.g., Aurelia (jellyfish). Some other cnidarians exist in both forms, i.e., polyp and medusa, e.g., Obelia. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms show alternation of generation in their life (metagenesis).

Match the following columns and select the correct option.

Column-I Column-II
(a) Gregarious, polyphagous pest (i) Asterias
(b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry (ii) Scorpion
(c) Book lungs (iii) Ctenoplana
(d) Bioluminescence (iv) Locusta
questions.solution:
Gregarious pest: A pest is an animal that is detrimental or harmful to humans or human concerns. Locusta (locust) is a pest that is dangerous to crops. It causes heavy damage to the vegetation. As it lives in groups of the same individuals but does not help one another, hence called gregarious.

Body symmetry of Echinoderms: The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical, but their larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. The echinoderms are unique in this feature that the larvae are bilaterally symmetrical (an advanced feature) while the adults developing from them are radially symmetrical (a primitive feature). Examples: Asterias (Starfish), Echinus (Sea urchin), Antedon (sea lily), Cucumaria (sea cucumber), and Ophiura (Brittle star).

Book-lungs: Present in scorpions, spiders, etc. These are the modified book-gills.

Bioluminescence: Bios means living and lumen means light. Bioluminescence is the property of production and emission of light by a living organism and hence shines in the dark background. It is a naturally occurring phenomenon. This property is well-marked in Ctenophores as they emit light and hence shine against the dark backgrounds. Examples: Pleurobrachia, Ctenoplana.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata?

(a) In Urochordata, notochord extends from head to tail, and it is present throughout their life.

(b) In Vertebrata, the notochord is present during the embryonic period only.

(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.

(d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata, and Cephalochordata.
questions.solution:
Fundamental characters of phylum chordates:
1. Presence of notochord: They are characterized by the presence of rod-like supporting notochord extending throughout the length of the body.
2. Presence of dorsal tubular nerve cord: They are characterized by the presence of dorsal nerve cord lying above the notochord.
3. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits: They are characterized by the presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits at some stage of their lifetime.
4. Presences of ventral heart: They are characterized by a ventral heart, i.e. heart is situated on the ventral side of the alimentary canal in the body cavity.
5. Presence of post-anal tail.
6. Body cavity: They are coelomates, Triploblsatic body, and bilaterally symmetrical animals.

Phylum Chordata is divided into three sub-phyla:
1. Urochordata (Gr: aura-tail): Here, the notochord is confined only to the tall region of the larva. It is represented by primitive chordates like Ascidia, Herdmania, commonly called ‘sea squirt’.
2. Cephalochordate (Gr: cephalon-head): Here, the notochord is well-developed, extending from the anterior to the posterior region of the body. Anteriorly, it extends beyond the nerve cord. Hence, the name cephalochordate. It includes primitive chordates like Amphioxus. Since the above two subphyla include primitive chordates, they are also called Protochordata.
3. Vertebrata or Craniata: Here, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column.

questions.q: Which one of the following groups of animals reproduces only by sexual means?
questions.solution:
In Ctenophores, asexual reproduction is absent. They are monoccious and fertilization is external. In cnidaria, asexual reproduction by budding is seen in polyp forms, and sexual reproduction in medusae forms. In protozoan, asexual reproduction occurs by fission, budding, etc. and sexual reproduction by conjugation and syngamy. In porifera ascxual reproduction occurs by gemmule formation.
Related Theory
Ctenophores are free-swimming. marine, solitary, pelagic animals with no polymorphism and no attached stages were found. They have a pair of long, solid, retractile tentacles and lack nematocysts. They have special adhesive and sensory cell i.e., colloblasts or lasso cells present in tentacles which helps in food capture. They are monoecious (hermaphrodite); gonads are endodermal situated on walls of digestive canals and development is direct with characteristic cydippid larva and lack asexual reproduction and alternation of generation. Regeneration and paedogenesis are common in them. Eg. Pleurobrachia, Hormiphora, Ctenoplana, Coeloplana.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sharks and dogfishes differ from skates and rays because:
options: head and trunk are widened considerably
distinct demarcation between body and tail
their pectoral fins distinctly marked off from cylindrical bodies.
questions.solution:
Sharks and dogfishes have cylindrical body while skates and rays have both of their pectoral fins fused. It gives a wing-like appearance and are not distinct from body.
Related Theory
Sharks have a pectoral fin behind the head on either side of its body. These are ofien elongated and are used to keep the shark from sinking to the bottom of the ocean, as well as for steering the fish. The shark's fins are rigid and elongated. They are supported by cartilaginous, non-segmented rods called ceratotrichia. This strength and rigidity helps the animal to move swifly and with agility. particularly useful when in pursuit of prey that darts away. Rays have flattened disk-like bodies with five gills exit openings and their mouth generally located on their underside. They have large pectoral fins, which they move like wings to travel in the water, and their tails are generally long and slender. with many species having one or more sharp, venomous spines that can be used to inflict painful wounds.

questions.q: Which one of the following statements is totally wrong about the occurrence of notochord, while the other three are correct?
options: It is present only in larval tail in Ascidians
It is replaced by a vertebral column in adult frog
It is absent throughout life in humans from the very beginning
It is present throughout life in Amphioxus
questions.solution: The notochord is a flexible, rod-shaped body found in embryo of all chordates. It is composed of cells derived from the mesoderm. It represents the primitive axis of embryo. In some chordates, it persists throughout life as the main axial support of the body (e.g., Amphibians), while in most vertebrates including humans it becomes the vertebral body of the vertebral column.

options: Penguin is homoiothermic while the remaining three are poikilothermic

Spongilla has special collared cells called choanocytes, not found in the remaining three
questions.solution: Spongilla belongs to phylum-Porifera, in which, choanoytes are the characteristic cells, these are absent in leech, dolphin and pengiun. These distinctive cells line the interior body walls of sponges. These cells have a central flagellum that is surrounded by a collar of micovilli. Choanocytes are versatile cells. Their flagella beat to create the active pumping of water through the sponge, while the collars of the choanocytes are the primary areas where nutrients are absorbed into the sponge.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the following has an open circulatory system?
questions.solution:
The Periplaneta has an open circulatory system, which means that blood does not flow through blood vessels and instead flows through haemocoel (body cavity). All vertebrates and annelids (such as earthworms) and cephalopods (squids and octopus), have closed circulatory system.
Related Theory
In all vertebrate organisms, as well as some invertebrates, this is a closed-loop system in which the blood is not moving freely in a cavity. In a closed circulatory system, blood is contained inside blood vessels, circulating unidirectionally (in one direction) from the heart around the systemic circulatory route, then returning to the heart again. In contrast to a closed system, arthropods (including insects, crustaceans, and most mollusks) have an open circulatory system. In an open circulatory system, the blood is not enclosed in the blood vessels, but is pumped into a cavity called a hemocoel. The blood is called haemolymph because it mixes with the interstitial fluid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which of the following notochord is present in the embryonic stage?
questions.solution: All chordates have a notochord present in the embryonic stage. In Tunicates, the notochord is present only in the larval stage, being completely absent in the adult animal. Urochordates, like Herdmania have notochord and nerve cord present only in tail. Tadpole undergoes retrogressive metamorphosis and notochord and nerve cord is absent in adults, which is lost during metamorphosis. In vertebrates the notochord develops into the vertebral column, becoming vertebrae and the intervertebral discs the centre of which retains a structure similar to the original notochord.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In which animal the nerve cell is present but the brain is absent?
questions.solution:
Hydra which belongs to the phylum coelenterata has nerve cells but no brain. Its nervous system consists of nerve cells and their processes.
Sponges are the only multicellular animals without a nervous system. They do not have any nerve cells or sensory cells.
Earthworms have a simple nervous system. The cerebral ganglion is connected to a ventral nerve cord that runs the length of the body.
Cockroach has in total 9 ganglia in number. Each ganglion of the nerve cord is formed by the fusion of two ganglia except the ganglion in the 7th segment.
Related Theory
The nervous system of the cockroach is spread throughout the body. The head holds a bit of nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral (belly-side) part of its body. So, if the head of the cockroach is cut off, it will still live for as long as one week.
Caution
Here brain word implies any kind of nerve tissue agglomerations/ganglion. All the options given lacks brain.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not a primary characteristic used for classifying animals?
questions.solution: Inspite of differences in structure and form of different animals, there are fundamental features common to various individuals in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems. These features are used as the basis of animal classification Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. Some division of labour (activities) occur among the cells. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. A still higher level of organisation, i.e., organ level is exhibited by members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What are the animals called which have no body cavity?
questions.solution: Presence or absence of a cavity between the body wall and the gut wall is very important in classification. The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom. Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordates. In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g., aschelminthes. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic animals, e.g., coelenterates. An undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the common name for members of the phylum that sponges belong to?
questions.solution: The common name for members of the phylum that sponges belong to is Porifera.Sponges are generally marine animals and are typically found in marine environments.Sponges have a water transport or canal system. Water enters through minute pores (ostia) in the body wall into a central cavity, spongocoel, from where it goes out through the osculum. This pathway of water transport is helpful in food gathering, respiratory exchange and removal of waste. Choanocytes or collar cells line the spongocoel and the canals. Digestion is intracellular. The body is supported by a skeleton made up of spicules or spongin fibres. Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite), i.e., eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual. Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation and sexually by formation of gametes. Fertilisation is internal and development is indirect having a larval stage which is morphologically distinct from the adult.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the function of cnidoblasts in cnidarians?
questions.solution: Cnidoblasts, also known as cnidocytes, contain stinging capsules or nematocysts and are used for anchorage, defense, and prey capture in cnidarians. Cnidarians exhibit tissue level of organization and are diploblastic.They have a central gastro-vascular cavity with a single opening, mouth on hypostome. Digestion is extracellular and intracellular. Some of the cnidarians, e.g., corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate. Cnidarians exhibit two basic body forms called polyp and medusa (Figure 4.6). The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the body shape of Aschelminthes?
questions.solution: The body of Aschelminthes is circular in cross-section, hence the name roundworms. Aschelminthes may be freeliving, aquatic and terrestrial or parasitic in plants and animals. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.Fertilization is internal in Aschelminthes.They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic and pseudocoelomate animals. Alimentary canal is complete with a well- developed muscular pharynx. An excretory tube removes body wastes from the body cavity through the excretory pore. Sexes are separate (dioecious), i.e., males and females are distinct. Often females are longer than males. Fertilisation is internal and development may be direct (the young ones resemble the adult) or indirect.

questions.q: What type of muscles do annelids possess to help in locomotion?
questions.solution: They may be aquatic (marine and fresh water) or terrestrial; free-living, and sometimes parasitic. They exhibit organ-system level of body organisation and bilateral symmetry. They are triploblastic, metamerically segmented and coelomate animals. Their body surface is distinctly marked out into segments or metameres and, hence, the phylum name Annelida (Latin, annulus : little ring). A closed circulatory system is present. Nephridia (sing. nephridium) help in osmoregulation and excretion. Neural system consists of paired ganglia (sing. ganglion) connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What phylum do insects belong to?
questions.solution: Insects belong to the phylum Arthropoda, which is the largest phylum of Animalia and includes over two-thirds of all named species on earth.The body of arthropods is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton. They have organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic, segmented and coelomate animals. The body consists of head, thorax and abdomen. They have jointed appendages (arthros-joint,poda-appendages). Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system. Circulatory system is of open type. Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts or balancing organs are present. Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules. They are mostly dioecious. Fertilisation is usually internal. They are mostly oviparous. Development may be direct or indirect.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the main distinctive feature of echinoderms?
questions.solution: These animals have an endoskeleton of calcareous ossicles and, hence, the name Echinodermata (Spiny bodied, All are marine with organ-system level of organisation. The adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but larvae are bilaterally symmetrical. They are triploblastic and coelomate animals. Digestive system is complete with mouth on the lower (ventral) side and anus on the upper (dorsal) side. An excretory system is absent. Sexes are separate. Reproduction is sexual. Fertilisation is usually external. Development is indirect with free-swimming larva.The most distinctive feature of echinoderms is the presence of water vascular system which helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration. Levels of organizationDescription
A. Cellular Level1. Cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues.
B. Tissue Level2. Tissues are grouped together to form organs with specific functions.
C. Organ Level3. Organs form functional systems for physiological processes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In non-chordates, if a heart is present, it is located dorsally.
Reason (R): Non-chordates possess a central nervous system that is ventral, solid, and double.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is a true statement. According to the fundamental features of animal phyla, non-chordates have a dorsal heart (if present), unlike chordates which have a ventral heart.

Reason (R) is also a true statement. The central nervous system in non-chordates is characteristically ventral, solid, and double, whereas in chordates it is dorsal, hollow, and single.

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A). The position of the heart and the position of the central nervous system are independent defining morphological characteristics of non-chordates. The ventral position of the nerve cord does not causally explain the dorsal position of the heart.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Match List-I with List-II regarding the fate or presence of the notochord.

List-IList-II
A. Urochordata(i) Notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult
B. Cephalochordata(ii) Notochord is present only in the larval tail
C. Vertebrata(iii) Notochord extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout life
D. Hemichordata(iv) Notochord is absent, but a rudimentary stomochord is present


Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
According to NCERT:
- In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail (A-ii).
- In Cephalochordata, it extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout life (B-iii).
- In Vertebrata, the notochord is present during the embryonic period and is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult (C-i).
- Hemichordata was earlier considered a subphylum under Chordata, but it is now a separate phylum of non-chordates. They lack a true notochord and instead have a rudimentary structure called a stomochord in the collar region (D-iv).

Therefore, the correct matching is A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv).

Answer: A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: While studying a marine animal, a biologist observes that a solid, rod-like supporting structure is present exclusively in the tail region of its larval stage and completely disappears in the adult form. Identify the subphylum to which this animal belongs, along with a correct representative example.
questions.solution:
In the subphylum Urochordata (also known as Tunicata), the notochord is present only in the larval tail and is lost during retrogressive metamorphosis into the adult form.

Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum are examples of Urochordata given in NCERT.

Cephalochordates (e.g., Branchiostoma) retain the notochord from head to tail throughout life. Vertebrates (e.g., Petromyzon) have the notochord replaced by a vertebral column. Hemichordates (e.g., Balanoglossus) possess a stomochord in the collar region, not a true notochord.

Answer: Urochordata; Ascidia

questions.solution:
According to NCERT, all members of the phylum Chordata possess a notochord at some stage of their life. The subphylum Vertebrata is a part of Chordata, so all vertebrates are chordates.

However, in vertebrates, the notochord is present only during the embryonic period and is later replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. Other chordates (like Urochordates and Cephalochordates, collectively called protochordates) never develop a vertebral column. Therefore, all chordates are not vertebrates.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, and (R) correctly explains why (A) is true.

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Taxonomists have classified certain animals into two groups based on their skeletal support:

Group A includes all animals that possess a notochord at some stage of their life cycle.
Group B includes animals that possess a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column.

It is observed that all members of Group B belong to Group A, but the reverse is not true. Which of the following developmental events correctly explains this observation?
options: The vertebral column in Group B is formed by the calcification of the dorsal hollow nerve cord.
Organisms in Group B possess both a notochord and a vertebral column simultaneously throughout their adult life.
Organisms in Group B possess a notochord during their embryonic period, which is replaced by a vertebral column in adults.
Organisms in Group A lose their notochord during embryonic development before forming a vertebral column.
questions.solution:
Group A represents the Phylum Chordata, while Group B represents the Subphylum Vertebrata.

Members of Vertebrata possess a notochord during the embryonic period. This notochord is later replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult stage. Because they have a notochord at some stage of their life cycle, they are included in Group A (Chordata).

However, protochordates (such as Urochordata and Cephalochordata) belong to Group A but never develop a vertebral column, which is why the reverse is not true.

The nerve cord does not calcify to form the vertebral column, and vertebrates generally do not retain the full notochord alongside the vertebral column in adulthood. Protochordates in Group A do not form a vertebral column at all.

Answer: Organisms in Group B possess a notochord during their embryonic period, which is replaced by a vertebral column in adults.

Read the following statements regarding the members of Class Reptilia:

(i) They are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.
(ii) They do not have external ear openings; the tympanum represents the ear.
(iii) The heart is usually three-chambered, but four-chambered in crocodiles.
(iv) Fertilisation is internal, they are oviparous and development is indirect.

questions.solution:
Statement (i) is correct. Reptiles are mostly terrestrial animals and their body is covered by dry and cornified skin, epidermal scales or scutes.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. While fertilisation is internal and they are oviparous, development in reptiles is direct, meaning there is no larval stage.

Therefore, exactly three statements are correct.

Answer: Three

questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully.

(a) Sponges possess a water vascular system which helps in food gathering and respiratory exchange.
(b) Cnidoblasts are used for anchorage, defense, and capture of prey in Coelenterates.
(c) Annelids are pseudocoelomate animals with bilateral symmetry.
(d) Radula is a file-like rasping organ for feeding present in Mollusca.
(e) Arthropods possess a closed circulatory system.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Statement (a) is incorrect because sponges (Porifera) possess a water canal system, not a water vascular system (which is a characteristic feature of Echinoderms).

Statement (b) is correct as cnidoblasts (or cnidocytes) present on the tentacles and body of cnidarians are used for anchorage, defense, and capturing prey.

Statement (c) is incorrect because annelids are true coelomates, whereas aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates.

Statement (d) is correct as the mouth of molluscs contains a file-like rasping organ for feeding called the radula.

Statement (e) is incorrect because arthropods have an open circulatory system.

Thus, only statements (b) and (d) are correct.

Answer: (b) and (d) only

Statement (E) is incorrect: Although fertilisation is internal, birds are oviparous (egg-laying), not viviparous.

Therefore, exactly three statements ((A), (B), and (D)) are correct.

Answer: Three

Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Petromyzon dies within a few days after spawning in fresh water.
Reason (R): Petromyzon is a marine organism that migrates to fresh water for spawning.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation for Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.
Assertion is correct but Reason is incorrect.
Assertion is incorrect but Reason is correct.
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct because Petromyzon (a cyclostome) migrates to fresh water to spawn and dies within a few days after the process.
Reason (R) is also correct because cyclostomes are marine organisms that exhibit anadromous migration (migrating from marine to fresh water for spawning).

However, Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A). The migration to fresh water is a prerequisite for spawning, but the actual cause of death is the physiological exhaustion and changes following the spawning event, not merely the fact that it is a marine organism migrating to fresh water.

Therefore, both Assertion and Reason are correct, but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

Answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct but Reason is not the correct explanation for Assertion.

questions.q: Which of the following statements correctly describes a fundamental anatomical difference between Periplaneta (cockroach) and Rana (frog)?
options: Rana possesses a dorsal heart, whereas Periplaneta possesses a ventral heart.

Periplaneta possesses a dorsal, hollow nerve cord, whereas Rana possesses a ventral, solid nerve cord.
Periplaneta possesses a dorsal heart, whereas Rana possesses a ventral heart.
questions.solution:
Periplaneta (cockroach) belongs to the phylum Arthropoda, which is a non-chordate group. In non-chordates, if a heart is present, it is located dorsally, and the central nervous system is ventral, solid, and double.

Rana (frog) belongs to the class Amphibia, which is a chordate group. Chordates are characterized by a ventral heart and a dorsal, hollow, and single central nervous system.

Therefore, Periplaneta has a dorsal heart while Rana has a ventral heart. The other options incorrectly assign or swap these fundamental chordate and non-chordate features.

Answer: Periplaneta possesses a dorsal heart, whereas Rana possesses a ventral heart.

Assertion (A): Ornithorhynchus and Aptenodytes are both oviparous animals.

Reason (R): Ornithorhynchus is a mammal whereas Aptenodytes is a bird.

options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.solution:

However, Reason (R) does not explain Assertion (A). The fact that Ornithorhynchus is a mammal does not explain why it is oviparous (since most mammals are viviparous). The correct explanation for their oviparity lies in their specific evolutionary history.

Thus, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A marine vertebrate migrates to fresh water for spawning. After spawning, within a few days, it dies. Its larvae, after metamorphosis, return to the ocean. Which of the following morphological features is characteristic of this animal?
options: Presence of placoid scales and claspers in males
Body is devoid of scales and paired fins
Presence of ctenoid scales and an air bladder
questions.solution:
The life cycle described (migration to fresh water for spawning, death after spawning, and larval metamorphosis before returning to the ocean) is a characteristic feature of class Cyclostomata (e.g., Petromyzon).

Members of Cyclostomata have an elongated body, a sucking and circular mouth without jaws, and their body is devoid of scales and paired fins.

Placoid scales and claspers are features of Chondrichthyes.

Ctenoid scales and an air bladder are features of Osteichthyes.

A three-chambered heart and moist skin are features of Amphibia.

Answer: Body is devoid of scales and paired fins

questions.q: In certain animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm. Instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Which of the following organisms exhibits this specific body plan?
questions.solution:
The body cavity described is a pseudocoelom, where the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm. Animals possessing a pseudocoelom are called pseudocoelomates. According to NCERT, members of the phylum Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates.

Ascaris belongs to Aschelminthes and is therefore a pseudocoelomate.

Fasciola belongs to Platyhelminthes, which are acoelomates (lacking a body cavity).
Pheretima is an annelid and is a true coelomate.
Adamsia is a cnidarian, which is diploblastic and lacks a mesoderm entirely.

Answer: Ascaris

questions.q: An elongated marine vertebrate 'X' is found acting as an ectoparasite on some fishes. It possesses a closed circulatory system and a cartilaginous cranium and vertebral column. Which of the following represents a correct characteristic of animal 'X'?
options: It possesses tough skin containing minute placoid scales.

questions.solution:

The other options are incorrect because Cyclostomes are devoid of scales and paired fins (placoid scales are found in Chondrichthyes), they migrate from marine to fresh water (not the reverse), and they have a sucking and circular mouth without jaws (powerful jaws are a feature of Gnathostomata like Chondrichthyes).

Answer: Its larvae return to the ocean after undergoing metamorphosis.

Given below are some statements regarding different animals:
A. Physalia exhibits tissue level of organisation and is triploblastic.
B. Pheretima possesses a true coelom and a double ventral nerve cord.
C. Sycon has a water vascular system.
D. Macropus is homoiothermous and viviparous.
E. Hippocampus has a cartilaginous endoskeleton.

Select the correct statements from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect. Physalia belongs to the phylum Coelenterata (Cnidaria), which exhibits tissue level of organisation but are diploblastic animals.

Statement B is correct. Pheretima belongs to the phylum Annelida. Annelids are true coelomates and possess a neural system with a double ventral nerve cord.

Statement C is incorrect. Sycon belongs to the phylum Porifera, which possesses a water transport or canal system. The water vascular system is a characteristic feature of Echinoderms.

Statement D is correct. Macropus belongs to the class Mammalia. Mammals are homoiothermous (warm-blooded) and Macropus is viviparous.

Statement E is incorrect. Hippocampus belongs to the class Osteichthyes (bony fishes), which possess a bony endoskeleton, not a cartilaginous one.

Therefore, only statements B and D are correct.

Answer: B and D only

(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:

Reason (R) is also correct and explains the Assertion: These anatomical features are crucial flight adaptations. Pneumatic bones make the body lighter, while air sacs supplement respiration to provide the high amount of oxygen required for the energy-intensive process of flight.

Therefore, both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

Read the following statements carefully:

(ii) Ctenophores reproduce only by sexual means.
(iii) In Annelids, the neural system consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord.
(iv) Molluscs have a segmented body with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump.
(v) In Hemichordates, the circulatory system is of open type.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (i) is incorrect. In phylum Porifera (sponges), digestion is strictly intracellular.

Statement (ii) is correct. In phylum Ctenophora, reproduction takes place only by sexual means.

Statement (iii) is correct. Annelids possess a neural system consisting of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord.

Statement (iv) is incorrect. Molluscs have an unsegmented body with a distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump.

Statement (v) is correct. Hemichordates have an open type of circulatory system.

Thus, statements (ii), (iii), and (v) are correct. There are three correct statements in total.

Answer: Three

Therefore, exactly three animals (Columba, Aptenodytes, and Neophron) belong to Class Aves and possess a crop and gizzard. Students often mistakenly include Pteropus because it flies, but it is a mammal.

Answer: 3

Assertion (A): All chordates are vertebrates but all vertebrates are not chordates.

Reason (R): In vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult, whereas protochordates lack a vertebral column.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true but Reason is false.
Assertion is false but Reason is true.
questions.solution:
According to NCERT, all vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. This is because all members of the subphylum Vertebrata possess a notochord during the embryonic period, which is later replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. Protochordates (Urochordata and Cephalochordata) are chordates but they lack a vertebral column.

Therefore, the Assertion is false as it states the reverse relationship, while the Reason is a true statement.

Answer: Assertion is false but Reason is true.

questions.q: Which of the following sets of animals exhibit homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and possess mammary glands?
questions.solution:
The characteristics mentioned (homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and presence of mammary glands) are defining features of the class Mammalia.

Let us evaluate the given options:
Macropus (Kangaroo) and Camelus (Camel) are mammals, but Psittacula (Parrot) belongs to class Aves. Birds are homoiothermic and have internal fertilisation but lack mammary glands.
Ornithorhynchus (Platypus) is a mammal, but Crocodilus (Crocodile) is a reptile (poikilothermic, lacking mammary glands) and Neophron (Vulture) is a bird.
Pteropus (Flying fox), Delphinus (Common dolphin), and Equus (Horse) all belong to class Mammalia. Therefore, they all exhibit homoiothermy, internal fertilisation, and possess mammary glands.
Balaenoptera (Blue whale) is a mammal, but Pavo (Peacock) is a bird and Rana (Frog) is an amphibian (poikilothermic, external fertilisation, lacking mammary glands).

Answer: Pteropus, Delphinus, Equus

The other options are incorrect because both Cyclostomata and Chondrichthyes possess a cartilaginous endoskeleton (cranium and vertebral column) and both have a closed type of circulatory system. Furthermore, it is Chondrichthyes that possess paired fins, while Cyclostomes lack them.

Answer: Cyclostomes lack scales on their body, whereas Chondrichthyes possess tough skin with minute placoid scales.

questions.q:
How many of the following animals possess both an open circulatory system and Malpighian tubules as their excretory structures?

Apis, Bombyx, Locusta, Palaemon, Limulus, Pheretima, Pila
questions.solution:
The question requires identifying animals that possess both an open circulatory system and Malpighian tubules. Malpighian tubules are the characteristic excretory structures of insects.

Apis, Bombyx, and Locusta are insects (phylum Arthropoda) and possess both an open circulatory system and Malpighian tubules.

Palaemon is a crustacean (phylum Arthropoda) with an open circulatory system, but its excretory organs are antennal glands or green glands.

Limulus is an arthropod with an open circulatory system, but it lacks Malpighian tubules.

Pheretima is an annelid and has a closed circulatory system along with nephridia for excretion.

Pila is a mollusc with an open circulatory system, but it lacks Malpighian tubules (it uses feather-like gills for excretion).

Thus, only 3 animals (Apis, Bombyx, and Locusta) meet both criteria.

Answer: 3

Read the following statements carefully:
A. All chordates possess a dorsal solid nerve cord.
B. In vertebrates, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the embryonic stage.
C. Protochordates are exclusively marine animals.
D. In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement A is incorrect because chordates are characterised by the presence of a dorsal hollow nerve cord, not a solid one. Non-chordates typically possess a solid nerve cord.

Statement B is incorrect because in vertebrates, the notochord is present during the embryonic period and is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult stage, not the embryonic stage.

Statement C is correct as the subphyla Urochordata and Cephalochordata are often referred to as protochordates and are exclusively marine.

Statement D is correct because in Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from the head to the tail region and persists throughout their life.

Therefore, only two statements (C and D) are correct.

Answer: Two

Read the following statements carefully:



(A) Protochordates are exclusively marine.


(B) In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.

How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution:
Statement (A) is correct as protochordates (comprising Urochordata and Cephalochordata) are exclusively marine.

Statement (B) is correct because in Urochordata, the notochord is restricted to the larval tail, whereas in Cephalochordata it extends from head to tail.

Statement (C) is incorrect. Chordates are characterized by a dorsal, hollow, and single central nervous system. A ventral, solid, and double nerve cord is a distinguishing feature of non-chordates.

Statement (D) is incorrect. Hemichordata was earlier considered a subphylum under phylum Chordata, but it is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata.

Therefore, exactly two statements are correct.

Answer: Two

Chelone (Turtle) belongs to class Reptilia. It is poikilothermic but has a typical 3-chambered heart.

Crocodilus (Crocodile) belongs to class Reptilia. Reptiles are poikilothermic. While most reptiles have a 3-chambered heart, crocodiles are an exception and possess a 4-chambered heart. Thus, it fits both descriptions.

Answer: Crocodilus

questions.q: Consider the marine animals Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum. Which of the following statements correctly describes the central supporting axis (notochord) in these organisms?
options: It is present only in the larval tail and is lost in the adult.
It extends from head to tail and is persistent throughout their life.
It is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult stage.
It is completely absent at all stages of their life cycle.
questions.solution:
The organisms Ascidia, Salpa, and Doliolum are examples of the subphylum Urochordata (Tunicata).

A defining characteristic of Urochordata is that the notochord is present exclusively in the larval tail and does not persist in the adult stage.

Cephalochordates have a notochord extending from head to tail throughout life, while vertebrates have it replaced by a vertebral column in adults.

Answer: It is present only in the larval tail and is lost in the adult.

questions.solution: Lamprey (or Petromyzon) belongs to class cyclostomata. The lamprey has about \(1 \mathrm{~m}\). long greenish brown, cylindrical body with smooth, scaleless, slimy skin; anterior circular, jawless mouth; a single dorsal naris; seven pairs of circular gill slits; 2 dorsal fins and a tail fin. The fish like adult lives in the sea and is parasitic on fishes.

questions.solution: Ctenidium is a monopectinate gill situated on the right side of the branchial chamber. Ctenidium helps in respiration by beating of cilia, thus creating water current. questions.solution: Tapeworm belonging to Phylum Platyhelminthes, pinworms and roundworm belonging to Phylum Nematoda, are all endoparasites. They all are intestinal parasites. questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Solenocytes are the main excretory structures in
questions.solution:
Solenocytes (also called flame cells) are meant for excretion and osmoregulation in Platyhelminthes. Annelids have metanephridia for excretion. Molluscs have kidneys (although different from vertebrate kidneys) for excretion.
In echinodermates, no special excretory organs are found for excretion. In them, excretion takes place through diffusion or osmosis or through active transport.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Tube feet is the locomotory organ of
questions.solution: Tube feet are extensible tubular processes bearing suckers and present in rows on the under-surface of echinoderms. Tube feet are connected internally with water vascular system. Each tube foot has an ampulla, a podium and a sucker. Tube feet are sensory structures that take part in adhesion, locomotion, respiration and food capturing. They are locomotory organs of echinoderms like starfish. Jelly fish is a member of phylum-Coelenterata. Scoliodon is a fish and silver fish is an arthropod.

In birds, fishes and snakes, notochord is replaced by vertebral column.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Polyp phase is absent in
questions.solution:
Polyp and medusa are the asexual and sexual phase present respectively in coelenterates. The members of different classes can be differentiated by the presence or absence of these stages.
Aurelia (jelly fish) belongs to class-Scyphozoa, in which medusoid phase is dominant and polypoid phase absent.
Hydra, Obelia, Physalia are the members of class- Hydrozoa in which, both medusoid and polypoid stages are present.
Metridium, Tubipora etc., belong to classAnthozoa, with all polyps but no medusae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In Mollusca, eye is present over a stalk, called
questions.solution: In Mollusca, each eye is located upon a stumpy peduncle called ommatophore. In Mollusca, a loose skin fold, called mantle, dorsally covers most of the body and encloses a large mantle cavity. The mantle cavity contains the rectum, genital duct, a penis in males and a small bipectinate chemoreceptor called osphradium. In Mollusca, the large oval aperture or mouth of the shell can be tightly closed by a thick, plate-like operculum attached to the foot.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Turbellarians are free living
questions.solution: Turbellaria (L. turbella - a string) is a class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. Turbellarians are mostly free, living flat worms, majorly aquatic (marine), presence of cilia, body unsegmented, mouth ventral, suckers absent with tango, chemo and photoreceptors, eg, Planaria (Dugesia), Bipalium etc. Trematoda (Gr. trema = hole; eidos $=$ form), class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. Commonly called 'flukes', ecto or endoparasites, body without cilia, unsegmented with suckers and hooks, eg, Fasciola, Schistosoma etc.Cestoda (Gr. kestos $=$ girdle eidos $=$ form) is also one of the class of phylum-Platyhelminthes. They are commonly called 'tapeworms' parasites without cilia and sense organs body segmented (pseudometamerism), digestive system absent, eg, Taenia and Echinococcus.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The characteristic larva of phylum'Coelenterata' is
questions.solution: Coelenterata (coelom + enteron) or phylum Cnidaria shows both sexual and asexual reproduction. The larval stages areplanula (Obelia) andephyra (Aurelia).Cysticercus (bladder worm) is the third larval stage seen in Taenia besides oncosphere, hexacanth (other two larval stages). Cysticercus is seen after the hexacanth released in the stomach of pig, which, goes through blood circulation and on reaching muscles get encysted in the form of bladderworm.Rhabditiform is the first larval stage in Ascaris which is formed within $10-14$ days. It is non-infective juvenile stage which rests for a week and completes first moult within egg and becomes second stage rhabditiform larva which is infective. The larva is called rhabditiform or rhabditoid because of its close resemblance with Rhabditis.Wriggler is the larva of mosquito. It is free-swimming, active, aquatic larva performing wriggling movements. It has a life-span of 3-4 days.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Class Crustacea differs from Insecta in having :
questions.solution:
The main characteristics of class Crustacea and Insecta are as follows :
(1) Class Crustacea : Mostly aquatic with gills, two pairs of antennae and atleast three pairs of jaws, appendages mostly biramous and always more than four in the trunk region.
Example : prawn, crab, lobster etc.
(2) Class Insecta : Hexapod arthropods with a pair of antennae and three pairs of Jaws.
Example : cockroach, grasshopper, bees, housefly etc.

questions.q: Moulting hormone is secreted by
questions.solution: Moulting hormone (ecdysone) is secreted by prothoracic gland. These glands are paired, bilateral sheet of cells in the thorax. In Periplaneta, this endocrine gland is $X$-shaped. This gland is stimulated by prothoracicotropic hormone. Ecdysone, by causing transformation from larval to pupal stage, initiates post embryonic growth in insects.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not an insect?
questions.solution: Spider is not an insect. It belongs to the order Araneae of the class-Arachnida. It bears four pairs of walking legs unlike insects (have three pairs of walking legs). Loust, Lepisma and Termites are come in the category of insects.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which cells are found only in sponges?
questions.solution: Choanocytes are found only in sponges. The choanocyte is an ovoid cell with free ends bearing a transparent contractile collar. The collar surrounds a single, long flagellum. Choanocytes are used in feeding and for ensuring flow of water within the animal's body.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The scientist, who described the birds as glorified reptiles, was
questions.solution: Huxley stated that birds are glorified reptiles. The missing link Archaeopteryx is a fossil lizard bird. It was founded by Andreas Wagner (1861) from upper Jurassic limestone rocks of Solenbofen in Bowaria, Germany.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is left when bath sponges dries up?
questions.solution: Euspongia is called bath spongia. The sponge are classified on the basis of skeleton which is made up of spongin fibere. After the bath sponge dries only the skeleton is left.
